name: LTC6993IS6-1#TRMPBF
title: LTC6993-1/-2/-3/-4 TimerBlox monostable pulse generator (one-shot), 1 µs to 33.6 s, TSOT-23 and 2 mm × 3 mm DFN
summary: A one-shot timer: an edge on TRIG gives one output pulse whose width, 1 µs to 33.6 s, is set by a resistor on SET and a divider ratio chosen by the voltage on DIV. The DIV divider also chooses positive or negative pulses. Four versions cover rising or falling trigger edges, each retriggerable or not. It runs from 2.25 V to 5.5 V and its CMOS output sources or sinks 20 mA.
key_figures: 1 µs to 33.55 s, tOUT = NDIV • RSET / 50 kΩ • 1 µs
2.25 V to 5.5 V; 70 µA typ idle (RSET = 800k, NDIV ≤ 64, 5.5 V)
about 500 master periods (0.5 ms to 8 ms)
C 0 °C to 70 °C, I –40 °C to 85 °C, H –40 °C to 125 °C, MP –55 °C to 125 °C

notes: The digit after the dash is the version: -1 and -2 start a pulse on a rising TRIG edge, -3 and -4 on a falling edge; -2 and -4 can be retriggered, -1 and -3 cannot.
The letter after LTC6993 is the temperature grade (C, I, H, MP); DCB is the 2 mm × 3 mm DFN and S6 the TSOT-23. The marking does not carry the grade, which is on a label on the shipping container.
#TRMPBF codes are 500-unit reels; all codes are lead-free.
The #W codes are the automotive-grade parts, made under controlled manufacturing and AEC-Q100 qualified; only these are for automotive use.

pins.name: TRIG
pins.function: Trigger input. A rising edge starts a pulse on the LTC6993-1 and -2, a falling edge on the -3 and -4. The -2 and -4 restart the timing on each new edge during a pulse, so the pulse can be lengthened; the -1 and -3 ignore edges until the pulse has ended.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground. Tie it to a ground plane with low inductance.

pins.name: SET
pins.function: Pulse width set. Held at 1 V above GND; the current drawn out of it (ISET, 1.25 µA to 20 µA) sets the master oscillator. A resistor RSET to GND sets the width with the best accuracy; a 0.5 % or better metal or thin film part with 50 ppm/°C or better suits precise designs, a 1 % thick film part looser ones. Below about 500 nA the oscillator halts and a running pulse lasts until ISET returns. Keep capacitance on the pin below 10 pF for low jitter and stability; under 100 pF the VSET loop stays stable.

pins.name: DIV
pins.function: Divider and polarity select. An internal 4-bit converter reads VDIV as a fraction of V+ and turns it into DIVCODE, which sets NDIV and, through its top bit POL, the output polarity (POL = 0 positive pulses, POL = 1 negative pulses). Usually a 1 % divider from V+ to GND; keep the pin and its resistors away from OUT and other fast edges, and keep its capacitance under 100 pF so VDIV settles fast.

pins.name: V+
pins.function: Supply, 2.25 V to 5.5 V. Keep it quiet and decouple it to GND with 0.1 µF placed at the pins.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Output, swinging from GND to V+ through about 30 Ω. Driving an LED or any load of low impedance needs a series resistor that limits the current to 20 mA.

circuits.title: Envelope detector
circuits.description: An LTC6993-2 run from 3.3 V turns bursts of an 80 kHz carrier into a clean envelope signal. DIV is tied to GND (DIVCODE 0: NDIV = 1, positive pulses) and RSET = 800 kΩ gives a 16 µs pulse. Each carrier edge retriggers the pulse, so OUT stays high through a burst and drops 16 µs after its last edge.

circuits.title: Supply bypassing and layout connection
circuits.description: The connection behind the recommended board layouts for both packages: RSET from SET to GND sets the master period, R1 from V+ and R2 to GND bias DIV for the wanted DIVCODE (Table 1), and C1 = 0.1 µF ceramic decouples V+. TRIG is the trigger input and OUT the pulse output.

circuits.title: 100 µs negative pulse generator
circuits.description: The worked design example: an LTC6993-2 on 2.25 V to 5.5 V gives a 100 µs low-going pulse on each rising trigger edge, retriggerable. R1 = 102 k and R2 = 976 k select DIVCODE 14 (NDIV = 8, POL = 1); RSET = 625 k sets the width.
notes: 625k is not a standard 1 % value: 619k shortens the pulse by 0.97 %, or 309k and 316k in series give it closely.

circuits.title: Voltage-controlled pulse width
circuits.description: RMOD from a control voltage VCTRL joins RSET at SET. VCTRL pushes or pulls current through RMOD, changing ISET and so the pulse width as Equation 3 gives. R1 and R2 set DIVCODE; C1 decouples V+.

circuits.title: Digitally controlled pulse width
circuits.description: A microprocessor loads a 12-bit LTC1659 DAC whose output drives SET through RMOD. Half of an LTC6078 buffers VSET as the DAC reference, so the DAC output follows any VSET drift and the width depends only on the code DIN and the resistors. SET cannot drive the REF input itself, because the reference current would shift the width.
notes: tOUT = (NDIV • RMOD / 50kΩ) • 1µs / (1 + RMOD/RSET – DIN/4096), DIN = 0 to 4095.

circuits.title: Missing pulse detector
circuits.description: A retriggerable LTC6993-2 with inverted output (DIVCODE 14: NDIV = 8, POL = 1) and RSET = 402 k has tOUT = 64 µs. A 25 kHz input retriggers it every 40 µs, so OUT stays low; when an input pulse is missing, the 64 µs runs out and OUT goes high until the next edge.

circuits.title: 1.5 ms radio control servo reference pulse generator
circuits.description: An LTC6991 oscillator makes a 20 ms frame period; each of its rising edges triggers an LTC6993-1 that gives a 1.5 ms pulse. The one-shot uses R1 = 1 M and R2 = 280 k (DIVCODE 3, NDIV = 512) and an RSET made of R8 = 143 k in series with a 10 k trimmer R6 for calibrating the 1.5 ms. A switch on the LTC6991 RST pin, pulled up by R7 = 10 k, stops the frames when open and runs them when closed to GND. Both chips run from 5 V with 0.01 µF decoupling.

parts.note: 1.5 ms calibration; wiper tied to the grounded end
open: reset; closed to GND: run

circuits.title: Pulse delay generator
circuits.description: Two LTC6993-1 one-shots in series reproduce a 10 µs input pulse 100 µs later. The first (R4 = 182 k, R5 = 976 k: DIVCODE 13, NDIV = 64, POL = 1; RSET R6 = 78.7 k) answers the input's rising edge with a 100 µs low-going pulse. The rising edge at the end of that pulse triggers the second (R1 = 976 k, R2 = 102 k: DIVCODE 1, NDIV = 8; RSET R3 = 61.9 k), which gives the 10 µs output pulse. Both run from 5 V.

circuits.title: RC servo pulse generator with controlled retrigger lockout interval
circuits.description: A trigger reaches the first LTC6993-1 through R9 = 10 k and starts a 1.5 ms pulse (R1 = 1 M, R2 = 280 k: DIVCODE 3, NDIV = 512; RSET R3 = 147 k). That pulse triggers a second LTC6993-1 set for 20 ms (R6 = 1 M, R7 = 392 k: DIVCODE 4, NDIV = 4096; RSET R4 = 243 k). Its output drives the gate of M1, a 2N7002 that shorts the trigger node to GND, so new triggers are blocked until 20 ms after the start of each 1.5 ms pulse. R5 = 100 k holds the gate low otherwise. Both run from 5 V.

circuits.title: Staircase generator with reset
circuits.description: Each input pulse adds a step to the voltage on C1 = 1 µF: U2 (LT1490), with D1 inside its feedback loop, takes the input through the R10/R6 divider and charges C1 through D1 and R11 = 2 k. U3, the other LT1490 half, amplifies the C1 voltage with gain 1 + R7/R8 to give VOUT. The input also triggers a retriggerable LTC6993-2 with inverted output set for 1.5 ms (R1 = 280 k, R2 = 1 M: DIVCODE 12, NDIV = 512, POL = 1; RSET R3 = 147 k), so its output stays low while pulses keep coming. If no pulse comes within 1.5 ms the output goes high, turns on U4 (2N7002) and empties C1, resetting the staircase. R9 = 100 k pulls the gate to GND. All parts run from 5 V.

circuits.title: Pulse stretcher
circuits.description: Turns an input pulse of 1 µs to 10 µs into a much longer output pulse whose width follows the input width. Q1 and Q2 (2N2907) form a current mirror referenced to the 2.5 V LT1009 and R6, charging C1 = 2200 pF to make a ramp. The input's rising edge starts an LTC6993-1 set for a 500 µs low-going pulse (R2 = 182 k, R5 = 976 k: DIVCODE 13, NDIV = 64, POL = 1; RSET R3 = 392 k), which turns Q3 off through R7 and lets C1 charge; at other times Q3 holds C1 empty. The input's falling edge triggers an LTC6993-3 (R14 = 976 k, R15 = 102 k: DIVCODE 1, NDIV = 8); its output, through R1 and Q4, pulls the mirror's emitter node low and stops the ramp, which is left at a voltage proportional to the input width. U4 (LT1638) buffers the ramp and drives the LTC6993-3 SET pin through R16 = 140 k, with R13 = 113 k to GND, so the output pulse width varies with the ramp voltage.

circuits.title: On-time programmable pulsed solenoid driver
circuits.description: A rising trigger edge makes an LTC6993-1 turn a 24 V, 100 mA solenoid on for 5 seconds. R1 = 1 M and R2 = 887 k select DIVCODE 7 (NDIV = 2^21) and RSET R3 = 118 k sets the 5 s. OUT drives a 2N2219A (Q1) through R4 = 2 k; D1 (1N4004) sits across the coil. The one-shot runs from 5 V.

circuits.title: Safety time-out relay driver
circuits.description: A train of enable pulses keeps a 12 V relay pulled in; 5 s after the last pulse it drops out. A retriggerable LTC6993-2 with R1 = 1 M, R2 = 887 k (DIVCODE 7, NDIV = 2^21) and RSET R3 = 118 k gives the 5 s time-out, restarted by every pulse. OUT drives a 2N2219A (Q1) through R4 = 10 k; the relay coil sits between 12 V and the collector with D1 (1N4148) across it.

circuits.title: Consecutive test sequencer
circuits.description: After an adjustable delay of 2 s to 30 s, three one-second test pulses follow one another. An LTC6994-1 delay block (R2 = 1000 k, R3 = 887 k on DIV; SET fed by R1 = 63.4 k to GND and R9 = 274 k from the wiper of the 25 k DELAY ADJUST potentiometer R10 between 5 V and GND) delays the rising start edge. Its rising output triggers an LTC6993-1 for TEST 1; the falling end of each test pulse triggers the next one-shot, an LTC6993-3, for TEST 2 and then TEST 3. The three one-shots share one DIV bias (R5 = 1000k, R4 = 681k) and each has RSET = 191 k.

parts.note: DELAY ADJUST, 5V end 30 s, GND end 2 s

notes: Misprint: R5 should run from 5 V to the shared DIV node, not from GND; 1000k over 681k gives DIVCODE 6 (NDIV = 262,144), which with RSET = 191 k makes the 1 s test pulses.

operation.text: Four versions differ only in the trigger input: the LTC6993-1 starts on a rising edge and is not retriggerable, the -2 starts on a rising edge and is retriggerable, the -3 starts on a falling edge and is not retriggerable, the -4 starts on a falling edge and is retriggerable. Every version can give positive or negative pulses, chosen by DIVCODE.

The SET pin is regulated to 1 V and the current drawn from it runs a master oscillator whose period is 1 µs per 50 kΩ of RSET. An edge on TRIG sets the output latch to its active state and starts the oscillator; a programmable divider (1, 8, 64, 512, 4096, 2^15, 2^18 or 2^21) counts master periods and resets the latch when the width is reached. Widths from 1 µs to 33.6 s are covered.

A V+-referenced 4-bit converter on DIV reads a divider and gives DIVCODE. The code picks NDIV and its top bit, POL, picks the output polarity: codes 8 and above give active-low pulses. Table 1 lists 1 % divider pairs for each code.
On the LTC6993-1 and -3, further trigger edges have no effect until the pulse has finished and a short rearm time tARM has passed. Trigger pulses, high and low, need a width of tWIDTH or more.

On the LTC6993-2 and -4 each new trigger edge restarts the timing, so the output stays active for tOUT past the final edge and a steady train of edges can hold it active for ever. Edges closer together than tRETRIG are not seen.

The converter keeps watching VDIV after start-up but reacts slowly so that the code cannot wander: a new code is taken only once it is stable, goes straight to the new value without passing through codes in between, and arrives after about 16 • (∆DIVCODE + 6) master periods. A pulse running during the change can end up with a width between the two settings. With an LTC6993-1 at V+ = 3.3 V and RSET = 200 kΩ, a step from code 0 to code 2 (and back) is taken up 512 µs after the DIV change, the pulse width going from 4 µs to 256 µs (and back).

At power-up the power-on reset starts a start-up period tSTART of about 500 master periods (0.5 ms to 8 ms) during which OUT is held low and triggers are ignored. The DIV converter has to settle on a code before any pulse can be made, so unstable supply or DIV voltage lengthens start-up; DIV capacitance below 100 pF does not. At the end, OUT goes high if POL = 1 and stays low if POL = 0, and the part is ready for trigger edges.

1: choose POL (codes 8 and above give negative pulses). 2: choose the version from the trigger edge and whether retriggering is wanted. 3: choose NDIV within tOUT/16 µs to tOUT/1 µs, the lowest for least current, then read the divider for the code from Table 1. 4: compute RSET = 50 kΩ • tOUT / (1 µs • NDIV) and take the nearest standard value. Worked example: a 100 µs negative pulse from a rising, retriggerable input at least current uses the LTC6993-2 with POL = 1; 6.25 ≤ NDIV ≤ 100 allows 8 or 64, and NDIV = 8 (DIVCODE 14, R1 = 102 k, R2 = 976 k) is chosen; RSET = 625 k, for which 619 k (a –0.97 % shift) or 309 k and 316 k in series can be used.

operation.topic: Voltage and digital control of width
operation.text: A resistor RMOD from a control voltage into SET adds or removes current and so moves the pulse width (Equation 3). When a DAC makes the control voltage, a buffered copy of VSET used as the DAC reference removes VSET drift from the result; SET cannot feed the DAC reference directly because the reference input current would change the width. Following a halving or doubling of ISET the width settles within 1 % in about six master periods; an LTC6993-1 at V+ = 3.3 V, DIVCODE 0, RSET = 200 kΩ, RMOD = 464 kΩ, stepping between 3 µs and 6 µs, shows this.

The oscillator is most accurate between 62.5 kHz and 1 MHz, which is ISET from 1.25 µA to 20 µA. Below 1.25 µA it still runs with less accuracy; near 500 nA it stops, and a pulse can start but does not end until ISET rises again. Running the oscillator above 2 MHz is not recommended because the DIV converter loses accuracy.

SET reacts to current changes almost at once, which makes it pick up coupling from fast signals such as TRIG. Some coupling always remains and is included in the NDIV = 1 accuracy figures; it makes the NDIV = 1 supply sensitivity depend on the trigger edge and, less, on output polarity. A poor layout makes it worse: route SET away from TRIG and other fast, large-swing lines.

The idle current IS(IDLE) depends on tOUT and V+. While timing, the current rises to IS(ACTIVE); the mean rise is proportional to the output duty cycle (time active over total time) and is smaller at larger NDIV.

Recommended for a 2-layer board with ground under and around the part, with 0603 passives: a 0.1 µF ceramic C1 straight across V+ and GND on a low-inductance path (on the TSOT-23, OUT may be routed between C1's pads so C1 reaches GND directly, or several vias to the plane are used); passives on the top side; RSET right at SET with a short direct trace and taken straight back to the GND pin; a ground trace guarding SET; R1 and R2 close to DIV with short connections. SET is a current-summing node, so any current coupled into it moves the pulse width.
